title: Carmen Fields gets a job at the Boston Globe
summary: His daughter, a Lincoln University graduate, wins a Globe job by challenging the editor, and rises to assistant editor.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Her brother teases her about it and says,--but she's doing real well--he used to say you need somebody to take care of you, but she's doing very well. She was assistant editor the Boston Globe, the third largest newspaper.
She was that for three or four years, and doing real well, but she finished in mid-term from Jefferson City, Missouri,

Lincoln University and when she was waiting to get her diploma, she worked in TV and that had been really her love, TV. So she went on to get her masters and she went to Boston, she was admitted and checked out and her grades were nice, she was admitted into the University of Boston and when she finished there, she would send out her name looking for work and she said it looked like she was having trouble getting a job at what she wanted. She did have a TV offer in Miami and I think Atlanta or something and we wrote her brother and he said, oh, that's the same as New York City, it's a big city, I think you would like it. But some how or other she didn't want to be there, but in talking to one of her teachers, I don't know who it was, he asked her one day if she got a job yet and she told him no she hadn't, so he told her to go to the Boston Globe and tell the man that he told her to come, and of course she did and she said when she called on him, he said no one has any opening now and the conversation

went on, but in some way he said a little later or something I may have an opening for a black girl, and so she said, an opening for a black girl, but you don't have an opening. So the way he thought--she kidded me after this-- (inaudible). He kind of chastised her and so she said the man said the way you speak you don't think a black girl should have a job? She said I sure do.

He caught on real quick, and he said I'll tell you what, in a couple of weeks come back for an interview. So she came up for the interview and she got the job and she was very happy and she worked to be assistant editor.
